Geographic focus:

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references import/production trends since 2015, July 2025 tariff decision
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — tariff decision pending, midterm election pressure, ongoing inventory distortions
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — proposed 15% tariff from Jan 2027 rising to 30% in 2028, long-term copper demand growth projections to 2040

Synopsis:
The White House has stalled on a decision regarding refined copper tariffs, caught between the goal of reshoring domestic copper production and the inflationary risk such tariffs would pose to U.S. manufacturers and consumers ahead of midterm elections. Commerce Secretary Lutnick submitted a report to Trump by the June 30 deadline, but no final decision has been announced. Market anticipation of tariffs has already driven U.S. copper stockpiles to record levels and diverted global supply flows into the U.S., tightening international markets. A phased tariff structure of 15% (2027) rising to 30% (2028) is under consideration. The policy uncertainty itself is acting as a supply disruptor globally.
